elements.name: screen
elements.doc: The display itself, not a box in it. Wherever it is written, including inside a clipped box or a component a `<route>` names, it covers the device: it defaults to `position: fixed` with every inset at zero.

elements.name: view
elements.doc: A generic box, the element most markup is made of. Defaults to `display: block`, so give it `display: flex` to lay its children out.

elements.name: text
elements.doc: A run of text. A `<text>` inside a `<text>` is part of the same sentence, styled on its own (`Read the <text class="b">terms</text>`), and `<image>` or `<path>` inside one sits in the line as a box, placed by `vertical-align`. Two `<text>` siblings still **stack**: they are two paragraphs. `role="heading"` announces it as a heading.

elements.name: image
elements.doc: `src` resolves relative to the `.rux` file, not the working directory. PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP. With no CSS size it lays out at its intrinsic pixel size.

elements.name: path
elements.detail: vector geometry from SVG path data
elements.doc: `d` is SVG path data, in the element's own coordinates. Paint is CSS, not attributes: `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `stroke-linecap`, `stroke-linejoin`, `fill-rule`. With no CSS size it lays out at the size of its own geometry. `:d` binds an expression, and two paths with the same command sequence animate between one another under `transition: d`.

elements.name: button
elements.detail: a tappable box, announced as a button
elements.doc: A tappable box. `<view @tap>` is the same thing to the layout; `<button>` says so to the accessibility tree.

elements.name: input
elements.detail: text field, textarea, select, checkbox or radio
elements.doc: A text field by default. `type="textarea"` is multiline, `type="select"` a combo box, `type="checkbox"` and `type="radio"` carry live checked state. Bind it with `r-model`.

elements.name: slot
elements.detail: a component's hole for the caller's children
elements.doc: Renders whatever the caller wrote between the component's tags. Children written inside `<slot>…</slot>` are the default, used when the caller passed nothing.

elements.name: router
elements.doc: Renders the first `<route>` whose path matches. Leaves no box of its own: the matched view expands in its place.

elements.name: route
elements.detail: maps a path to a component
elements.doc: `<route path="/crew/:id" view="crew-detail" />`. Routes are tried in the order written and the first match wins, so `fallback` can sit anywhere among them.

globalAttributes.name: @tap
globalAttributes.detail: run script when this element is tapped
globalAttributes.doc: A click and a finger are the same event. `@tap="count += 1"` takes an expression, and the element becomes focusable and announces as tappable.

globalAttributes.name: @press
globalAttributes.detail: a finger or button went down
globalAttributes.doc: Runs when a press lands on this element. `event.x` / `event.y` are relative to the element, `event.pageX` / `event.pageY` to the window, and `event.width` / `event.height` are the element's own size; `event.touches` lists every finger down.

globalAttributes.name: @release
globalAttributes.doc: Runs on release, whether or not the press stayed still enough to be a tap.

globalAttributes.name: @longpress
globalAttributes.doc: Runs once, after the press has been held still for half a second.

globalAttributes.name: @swipe
globalAttributes.doc: Runs once at the end of a press that travelled far enough, fast enough. `event.direction` is `left`, `right`, `up` or `down`, and `event.totalX` / `event.totalY` are how far it came. A drag that ends as a flick fires this too.

globalAttributes.name: @drag
globalAttributes.doc: Runs at the start of a drag, on every move, and at the end. `event.phase` says which; `event.totalX` / `event.totalY` measure from where the press landed, `event.moveX` / `event.moveY` from the previous event. A `@drag` claims the finger, so the page under it does not scroll.

globalAttributes.name: class
globalAttributes.doc: Space-separated class names, matched by `.name` selectors. `:class` is the bound form.

globalAttributes.name: id
globalAttributes.doc: Matched by `#name` selectors, and by `query("#name")` from script.

globalAttributes.name: style
globalAttributes.doc: Inline CSS for this element. `:style` is the bound form.

globalAttributes.name: label
globalAttributes.doc: What a screen reader calls this element, in place of the text inside it. On an `<image>` or `<path>`, `alt` says the same.

globalAttributes.name: role
globalAttributes.doc: Honored for selectors (`[role="heading"]`) and for the accessibility tree. Matches case-insensitively.

globalAttributes.name: dir
globalAttributes.detail: which way its text and rows run
globalAttributes.doc: `ltr`, `rtl` or `auto`, inherited. Sets `direction`: flex rows, grid columns and `text-align: start` begin from the right under `rtl`, and logical properties such as `margin-inline-start` follow it. `auto` leaves a text to its first letter with a direction. A `direction` rule overrides it.

globalAttributes.name: to
globalAttributes.doc: Tapping navigates to this path, the element announces as a link, and it matches `:current` when it names the path you are on. `:to` is the bound form.

globalAttributes.name: @submit
globalAttributes.detail: the form was sent, and every field passed
globalAttributes.doc: On a `role="form"` only. Sent by a `<button type="submit">` inside it or by the action key in its last field. `event.values` maps each field's `name` (or its `r-model`) to its value.

globalAttributes.name: @invalid
globalAttributes.detail: the form was sent, and a field failed
globalAttributes.doc: On a `role="form"` only. Runs instead of `@submit`: the first failing field takes the caret and every field matches `:user-invalid` from then on. `event.errors` maps each failing field's name to a sentence saying why; `event.values` is as for `@submit`.

globalAttributes.name: @key
globalAttributes.doc: Runs while focus is on this element or inside it. `event.key` is the key by the browser's names (`"s"`, `"Enter"`, `"Escape"`), with `event.ctrl`, `shift`, `alt`, `meta`, `primary` (Ctrl, or Cmd on macOS) and `repeat`. **`false` takes the key**: no handler further out runs, and the shell does nothing with it. A focused text field handles the keys it uses (text, editing, its Ctrl chords) before the `@key`s around it.

globalAttributes.name: @close
globalAttributes.detail: the person asked to close the app
globalAttributes.doc: On the app's `<screen>` only. Runs when the window's close button is pressed, or Android's Back has no page left. **`false` keeps the app open**, as a route guard's `false` refuses; anything else lets it close, and one that fails lets it close too. Open your own "save changes?" and call `close()` from it. Must answer at once, so an `async fn` cannot refuse. Not asked on the web yet.

directives.name: r-for
directives.doc: `r-for="item in items"`. Pair it with `r-key` so reconciliation can match rows across a change.

directives.name: r-key
directives.doc: `r-key="item.id"`. Without it a keyed change is a rebuild, and input state inside a row moves to the wrong row.

directives.name: r-if
directives.doc: `r-if="count > 0"`. The element and its subtree are absent, not hidden, when false.

directives.name: r-elif
directives.doc: Follows an `r-if` sibling. The first branch whose condition holds renders.

directives.name: r-else
directives.doc: Follows an `r-if` or `r-elif` sibling, and renders when none of them held.

directives.name: r-show
directives.doc: `r-show="expanded"`. The element stays in the tree and keeps its state; it is only not painted. Prefer `r-if` when the subtree is expensive.

directives.name: r-model
directives.doc: `r-model="name"` on an `<input>`: typing writes the signal, and writing the signal updates the field.

directives.name: r-transition
directives.detail: animate the way in and out
directives.doc: On an `r-if` branch or a keyed `r-for` row: the element is held on screen while it leaves. Style the two sides with `:enter-from` and `:leave-to`; the element's own `transition` sets how long. `:r-transition="expr"` hands progress to you instead, 0 to 1.

image.name: src
image.doc: Resolved relative to the document, not the working directory. `:src` binds an expression.

image.name: alt
image.doc: What the image is, for the accessibility tree.

path.name: d
path.doc: The full SVG grammar: `M L H V C S Q T A Z`, absolute or relative. Coordinates are in the element's own box. `:d` binds an expression.

path.name: alt
path.doc: What the drawing shows. Without it the path is treated as decoration and left out of the accessibility tree.

input.name: type
input.detail: text | textarea | password | search | number | date | select | checkbox | switch | slider | radio
input.doc: Omitted means a single-line text field.

input.name: placeholder
input.detail: text shown while empty
input.doc: Shown until the field has a value. Not a label.

input.name: value
input.detail: the field's value
input.doc: The literal starting value. For state that changes, use `r-model`.

input.name: checked
input.detail: checkbox / radio state
input.doc: Live state for `type="checkbox"` and `type="radio"`, and matched by the `:checked` pseudo-class.

input.name: name
input.detail: radio group, and the key a form sends it under
input.doc: Radios sharing a `name` are one group, so choosing one clears the others. In a `role="form"`, `event.values` carries the field under this name; without one, under its `r-model`.

input.name: required
input.detail: must have a value to submit
input.doc: Valueless, or bound with `:required`. Empty text, or a checkbox or switch that is off, fails it. Matched by `:required`, and by `:invalid` while it fails.

input.name: minlength
input.detail: the fewest characters it takes
input.doc: Checked when its form is submitted, counted like `maxlength`. An empty field fails only `required`.

input.name: pattern
input.detail: a regular expression the value matches
input.doc: Matches the whole value, as HTML's does: `pattern="\d{4}"` takes `1906` and refuses `19064`. An empty field fails only `required`.

input.name: options
input.detail: the choices for a select
input.doc: For `type="select"`. `:options` binds an array.

input.name: disabled
input.detail: cannot be focused, tapped or changed
input.doc: On whenever it is written, so `disabled="false"` is still disabled: bind it with `:disabled="expr"` instead. Matched by `:disabled`. Also on `<button>`.

input.name: readonly
input.detail: can be selected and copied, not changed
input.doc: The caret and the selection work and no keyboard opens. `:readonly` binds it.

input.name: min
input.detail: the lowest value or earliest day
input.doc: A number for `type="slider"` (0 when left off), a `YYYY-MM-DD` day for `type="date"`. On `type="number"`, a check its form's submission makes.

input.name: max
input.detail: the highest value or latest day
input.doc: A number above `min` for `type="slider"` (100 when left off), a `YYYY-MM-DD` day for `type="date"`. On `type="number"`, a check its form's submission makes.

input.name: step
input.detail: what a slider's value moves by
input.doc: For `type="slider"`. 1 when left off; `any` for no steps. The value is rounded to as many decimal places as the step is written with.

input.name: maxlength
input.detail: the most characters it takes
input.doc: Counted as HTML counts them, in UTF-16 units. Typing past it is refused and a paste is cut short.

input.name: inputmode
input.detail: text | numeric | decimal | tel | email | url | search | none
input.doc: Which keyboard a phone raises. The field is still a text field and its value still text: a PIN or a phone number is `inputmode="numeric"`, not a number.

input.name: enterkeyhint
input.detail: enter | done | go | next | previous | search | send
input.doc: What the keyboard's action key says. `next` and `previous` move focus like Tab, `done` closes the field, and in a form every other one submits it; every one commits the field first, which fires `@change`. Left off in a form, it is `next` on each typing field and `go` on the last.

input.name: autocomplete
input.detail: what the field holds, for autofill
input.doc: HTML's field names: `username`, `current-password`, `new-password`, `email`, `tel`, `name`, `postal-code`, `cc-number`, `one-time-code` and the rest. A phone's password manager fills the fields of the focused field's form from them, and offers to save after `@submit`. `off` keeps the field away from autofill. Without it, a password, an email keyboard and a phone keyboard are recognised anyway.

input.name: autofocus
input.detail: take focus when it appears
input.doc: Valueless. Focuses the field when it first appears, a route or an `r-if` bringing it in included, unless something already has focus.

input.name: @input
input.detail: the text changed
input.doc: After every change, however it was made. `event.value` is the new text.

input.name: @change
input.detail: a changed value was committed
input.doc: When the field is left with a different value than it had, or Enter is pressed in a one-line field. A select fires it on choosing, a checkbox or radio on toggling. `event.value` is the value.

input.name: @focus
input.detail: the field gained focus
input.doc: `event.value` is its text.

input.name: @blur
input.detail: the field lost focus
input.doc: After `@change`, when both fire. `event.value` is its text.

button.name: disabled
button.doc: No `@tap`, no link, no gesture, and nothing for Tab to land on. On whenever it is written; `:disabled="expr"` binds it. Matched by `:disabled`.

button.name: type
button.doc: `submit` sends the `role="form"` around it once its own `@tap` has run: `@submit` if every field passes, `@invalid` if not. `button`, or leaving it off, is an ordinary button.

route.name: path
route.doc: `/crew/:id` captures `id` and hands it to the view as a prop. A child route's path is relative to its parent, and `path=""` is the index route that fills the parent's outlet at the parent's own path.

route.name: view
route.doc: Names an imported component. Either spelling: `view="crew-detail"` as the tag is written, or `view="crew_detail"` as the `use` that imports it is written. They are the same component.

route.name: name
route.detail: a name to build this route's path from
route.doc: `path_for("crew-detail", { id: "ada" })` builds the path from the name and the parameters, so a link survives the path being changed.

route.name: fallback
route.doc: Valueless. Renders when no other route matched, wherever it sits among them.

route.name: guard
route.detail: decide whether this route may be entered
route.doc: `guard="expr"`, run whenever this route is part of the match. `false` cancels the navigation, a string redirects to that path, and anything else allows it, `()` included, so a function that falls off the end has consented. Outer guards run first. In scope: `to`, `from`, the path's parameters, and `linked`, true when a deep link or a browser URL started the navigation rather than the app itself.

router.name: restore-scroll
router.doc: Puts a page back where it was when you return to it.

router.name: guard
router.detail: decide whether any navigation may proceed
router.doc: `guard="expr"`, run on every navigation this router handles, before the history moves. So a refusal leaves no entry behind, and Back and Forward pass through it too, not just `navigate`. `false` cancels, a string redirects, anything else allows.

text.name: for
text.doc: Names the `id` of the element this text labels, so the accessibility tree pairs them.

type.name: text
type.doc: The default, so `type` may be left off entirely.

type.name: textarea
type.doc: Enter inserts a newline instead of being ignored, and the box scrolls its own content.

type.name: password
type.doc: Shows bullets, refuses Copy and Cut, and asks a phone's keyboard not to learn what is typed. The bound signal holds the real text.

type.name: search
type.detail: a field whose action key searches
type.doc: A one-line field in every other respect.

type.name: number
type.doc: The bound signal always holds a number. While what is typed is not one yet (`-`, `1.`, nothing) the signal keeps its last number and the field shows the typing; leaving the field shows the number again. A phone raises a signed decimal keyboard.

type.name: date
type.doc: The bound signal holds `YYYY-MM-DD`, as HTML's does, or is empty. A phone opens the platform's date picker; a desktop types the date, and only a real day inside `min` and `max` reaches the signal.

type.name: select
type.doc: Shows the bound value and opens a list on tap. Takes its choices from `:options`.

type.name: checkbox
type.doc: No caret and no focus of its own: a tap flips the bound value, and `:checked` matches it. Space or Enter activates it when tabbed to.

type.name: switch
type.doc: A checkbox that draws as a track and a thumb and is announced as a switch. `:checked` matches it on; `accent-color` colours the track when on.

type.name: slider
type.doc: Bound to a number between `min` and `max`, in steps of `step`. A tap puts the thumb where it lands and a sideways drag moves it; a vertical swipe still scrolls the page. `@input` fires as it moves, `@change` when the finger lifts. `accent-color` colours it.

type.name: radio
type.doc: Radios sharing a `name` are one group, so choosing one clears the others. Carries the chosen value in `value`.

inputmode.name: numeric
inputmode.doc: PINs, codes, card and phone numbers: digit strings, not quantities.

inputmode.name: email
inputmode.doc: Also turns off autocapitalisation on most keyboards.

inputmode.name: search
inputmode.doc: The same field, with Search where Enter was.

inputmode.name: none
inputmode.doc: For an app that draws its own keys. The field still takes a hardware keyboard.

enterkeyhint.name: done
enterkeyhint.doc: Commits, then drops focus and the keyboard.

enterkeyhint.name: go
enterkeyhint.doc: Commits; what going means is the app's `@change`.

enterkeyhint.name: next
enterkeyhint.doc: Commits, then moves focus as Tab does.

enterkeyhint.name: previous
enterkeyhint.doc: Commits, then moves focus as Shift+Tab does.

enterkeyhint.name: search
enterkeyhint.doc: Commits; the search is the app's `@change`.

scriptGlobals.name: signal
scriptGlobals.doc: Declare a piece of reactive state.

scriptGlobals.name: computed
scriptGlobals.doc: Derived state, readable anywhere a signal is. A **declaration, not a call**: there is no `computed(|| …)`. Refreshing is one pass in declaration order, so a computed may read one declared above it and not below. Inside a component it runs per instance.

scriptGlobals.name: prop
scriptGlobals.doc: In a component: something its caller passes, as `:name="expr"` or `name="text"` on the tag. `prop size = 16;` gives a default, so the caller may leave it off; without one the caller must pass it. A **declaration, not state**: the component reads it and cannot write it. A tag writes a two-word prop kebab or snake alike, so `:id-of` reaches `prop id_of;`. Any attribute on a component tag that is not a declared prop, a listener or a directive is an error.

scriptGlobals.name: effect
scriptGlobals.doc: Runs when what it read changes, and once on load. A **block, not a call**: there is no `effect(|| …)`. It subscribes to what it actually read on its last run, and is never woken by its own writes.

scriptGlobals.name: mounted
scriptGlobals.doc: Runs once the document is on screen. Document level today; a component declaring one is warned.

scriptGlobals.name: unmounted
scriptGlobals.doc: Runs when the document stops being the one on screen.

scriptGlobals.name: query
scriptGlobals.doc: Find elements by CSS selector, in a handler, against the frame already laid out. Returns an **array**, so check `.length` or index it: a selector that matches nothing is an empty array, not an error. Only inside a handler, because a binding that read the tree would rebuild the tree it read.

scriptGlobals.name: navigate
scriptGlobals.doc: Go to a path, leaving the current one in the history.

scriptGlobals.name: replace
scriptGlobals.doc: Go to a path *without* a history entry. The only correct way to redirect.

scriptGlobals.name: back
scriptGlobals.doc: Walk back through the history.

scriptGlobals.name: forward
scriptGlobals.doc: Walk forward through the history.

scriptGlobals.name: pickFile
scriptGlobals.doc: Ask for one file with the platform's own dialog: its path, or `none` if cancelled. Awaited from an `async fn`. `filters` is `[{ name, extensions }]`. Throws `unsupported` on the web and Android for now.

scriptGlobals.name: pickFiles
scriptGlobals.doc: Ask for any number of files: their paths, `[]` if cancelled. Awaited from an `async fn`.

scriptGlobals.name: pickSaveFile
scriptGlobals.detail: await pickSaveFile({ title, filters, folder, name })
scriptGlobals.doc: Ask where to save, with the platform's own dialog: the path, or `none` if cancelled. `name` is the file name it suggests. Awaited from an `async fn`.

scriptGlobals.name: settings
scriptGlobals.doc: An app's own small values, kept between runs: `get` gives `any?` (`none` if never set), `set` writes at once, `remove` forgets. Kept per `[app] id`, in the platform's app-data folder (localStorage on the web).

scriptGlobals.name: close
scriptGlobals.doc: Close the app for good, without asking `@close` again: the app has decided. Every `unmounted` runs first. Does nothing on the web, where a page cannot close its own tab.

scriptGlobals.name: path_for
scriptGlobals.doc: Build a path from a named route and its parameters.

scriptGlobals.name: emit
scriptGlobals.doc: A component telling its caller something happened.

scriptGlobals.name: blur
scriptGlobals.doc: Drop focus. Free-standing rather than a method on an element, because there is only one focused element: blurring "this one" would either do nothing or take focus from something else.

scriptGlobals.name: setInterval
scriptGlobals.doc: Run a block on a period, handing back a handle. A **block, not a callback**: `setInterval(1000) { seconds++ }`. Stop it with `clearInterval(handle)`.

scriptGlobals.name: clearInterval
scriptGlobals.doc: Stop a timer started by `setInterval`. The handle is what `setInterval` returned.

scriptGlobals.name: print
scriptGlobals.doc: Printf-debugging. Reaches the dev overlay, not just stderr.

scriptGlobals.name: debug
scriptGlobals.doc: Like `print`, with the value's structure shown.

scriptGlobals.name: Number
scriptGlobals.doc: The whole text as a number, as JavaScript reads it: `Number("2")` is 2, `Number("")` is 0, `Number("12px")` is `NaN`. How a route parameter, which is always text, meets a numeric id.

scriptGlobals.name: parseInt
scriptGlobals.doc: The whole number that leads the text: `parseInt("42px")` is 42, and `parseInt("px")` is `none`, so read it with `??`: `parseInt(s) ?? 0`. The radix is optional.

scriptGlobals.name: parseFloat
scriptGlobals.doc: The number that leads the text: `parseFloat("12.5px")` is 12.5, and `parseFloat("px")` is `none`, where JavaScript says `NaN`.

scriptGlobals.name: Ok
scriptGlobals.doc: A `Result` that holds a value: `{ ok: true, value }`. Read it with `if r.ok { r.value }`, or `r.unwrap()`.

scriptGlobals.name: Err
scriptGlobals.doc: A `Result` that holds an error kept as an answer: `{ ok: false, error }`. `r.unwrap()` on it throws the error.

scriptGlobals.name: intDiv
scriptGlobals.doc: Division that keeps an `int`, cutting toward zero: `intDiv(7, 2)` is 3, where `7 / 2` is 3.5. Dividing by zero is an error.

scriptGlobals.name: String
scriptGlobals.doc: Any value as the text a `{{ }}` binding would show.

scriptGlobals.name: isNaN
scriptGlobals.doc: Whether a `float` is `NaN`, the answer `Number` gives for text that is not a number, and `0.0 / 0` gives.

elementProperties.name: id
elementProperties.doc: **Absent rather than empty** when it has none, so `el.id ?? "none"` reads the way it does everywhere else.

elementProperties.name: classes
elementProperties.doc: Every class on the element, in the order written.

elementProperties.name: x
elementProperties.doc: From the frame **currently on screen**, so it is one frame stale. That is the guarantee, not a defect: a handler runs before the next layout, exactly as `getBoundingClientRect` does. Absent when there is no frame yet, so "not laid out" stays distinguishable from "laid out and genuinely zero".

elementProperties.name: y
elementProperties.doc: See `x`: one frame stale, absent before the first layout.

elementProperties.name: width
elementProperties.doc: See `x`: one frame stale, absent before the first layout.

elementProperties.name: height
elementProperties.doc: See `x`: one frame stale, absent before the first layout.

elementMethods.name: focus
elementMethods.doc: Give this element keyboard focus. Recorded and applied **after the handler finishes**, so a handler that focuses something and then changes state does not race its own tree.

elementMethods.name: scrollIntoView
elementMethods.doc: Scroll whichever box scrolls until this element is visible. Applied after the handler, like the rest.

elementMethods.name: tap
elementMethods.doc: Tap this element as though a finger had. This is how a `mounted` hook drives the document, and how most of the lifecycle was verified.

valueMethods.name: map
valueMethods.doc: A new array, each item transformed. Returns; the receiver is untouched.

valueMethods.name: filter
valueMethods.doc: A new array of the items that passed.

valueMethods.name: reduce
valueMethods.doc: Fold the array to one value.

valueMethods.name: forEach
valueMethods.doc: Called with `(item, index)`, and falls back to `(item)`.

valueMethods.name: find
valueMethods.doc: The first item that passed, or absent.

valueMethods.name: findIndex
valueMethods.doc: Where the first item that passed is, or -1.

valueMethods.name: some
valueMethods.doc: Whether any item passes.

valueMethods.name: every
valueMethods.doc: Whether every item passes.

valueMethods.name: sort
valueMethods.doc: Sorts by the comparison and **returns** the sorted array, as JavaScript's does. The receiver is sorted too.

valueMethods.name: includes
valueMethods.doc: Whether the array or string contains it.

valueMethods.name: indexOf
valueMethods.doc: Where it first occurs, or -1.

valueMethods.name: slice
valueMethods.doc: A section, without changing the original.

valueMethods.name: split
valueMethods.doc: A string to an array of pieces.

valueMethods.name: join
valueMethods.doc: An array to one string.

valueMethods.name: charAt
valueMethods.doc: The character at an index.

valueMethods.name: repeat
valueMethods.doc: The string over again, n times.

valueMethods.name: startsWith
valueMethods.doc: Whether it begins with that.

valueMethods.name: endsWith
valueMethods.doc: Whether it ends with that.

valueMethods.name: trim
valueMethods.doc: **Returns** the trimmed string and leaves the receiver alone. rhai's own `trim` empties the string it was given and returns nothing, which rendered `{{ name.trim() }}` blank; Rux shadows it.

valueMethods.name: toLowerCase
valueMethods.doc: Returns a new string.

valueMethods.name: toUpperCase
valueMethods.doc: Returns a new string.

valueMethods.name: length
valueMethods.doc: A **property, not `len()`**, and only on arrays and strings.

pseudoClasses.name: hover
pseudoClasses.detail: the pointer is over this box
pseudoClasses.doc: Needs a layout region, so the shell can tell when the pointer enters and leaves it. There is no hover on a touch screen, so it can decorate and must not be the only way to reach something.

pseudoClasses.name: focus
pseudoClasses.doc: A field, a select or a `@tap` box, reached by tapping it or by walking the focus order with Tab. The element itself only, not its ancestors. For the ring, prefer `:focus-visible`, which leaves a tapped button alone.

pseudoClasses.name: focus-visible
pseudoClasses.doc: A field whenever it has focus; anything else only when the keyboard put focus there, so a button tapped with a finger shows nothing and the same button reached with Tab does. The default ring is this rule's `outline: auto`, so `outline: none` here removes it and any other `outline` replaces it.

pseudoClasses.name: active
pseudoClasses.detail: a press is down on this box
pseudoClasses.doc: Held between press and release, so it is the state a button uses to look pushed.

pseudoClasses.name: checked
pseudoClasses.detail: a checkbox or radio is on
pseudoClasses.doc: Resolved during the build from the input's live state, rather than supplied by the shell as `:hover` and `:active` are.

pseudoClasses.name: current
pseudoClasses.detail: this link names the path you are on
pseudoClasses.doc: Matches an element whose `to` is the route you are currently on. It is the nav highlight, without a signal to track it.

pseudoClasses.name: enter-from
pseudoClasses.detail: the frame an element enters from
pseudoClasses.doc: Under `r-transition`: the style the element holds for exactly one frame as it arrives, and animates away from. The *hidden* end of the animation goes here.

pseudoClasses.name: leave-to
pseudoClasses.detail: the state an element leaves to
pseudoClasses.doc: Under `r-transition`: the style the element animates towards while it is held on screen on its way out. `position: absolute` here takes it out of flow, so the rest of a list closes up under it rather than waiting.

pseudoClasses.name: disabled
pseudoClasses.detail: an input or button that is switched off
pseudoClasses.doc: Matches a `<input>` or `<button>` with `disabled` (or a truthy `:disabled`). Rux draws no default look for it, so this is where the dimming goes.

pseudoClasses.name: enabled
pseudoClasses.detail: an input or button that is not disabled
pseudoClasses.doc: Form controls only: a plain box is neither enabled nor disabled, as in CSS.

pseudoClasses.name: valid
pseudoClasses.detail: an input whose value passes its checks
pseudoClasses.doc: Matched from the start, as in CSS. A disabled or readonly input is neither valid nor invalid.

pseudoClasses.name: invalid
pseudoClasses.detail: an input whose value fails a check
pseudoClasses.doc: `required`, `minlength`, `pattern`, a number's `min`/`max`, or the shape `inputmode="email"` or `"url"` implies. Matched from the start, so an empty required field is invalid before anyone has touched it: `:user-invalid` waits.

pseudoClasses.name: user-valid
pseudoClasses.detail: valid, once the person has been through it
pseudoClasses.doc: Like `:valid`, but only after the field was changed and left, or its form's submission was tried.

pseudoClasses.name: user-invalid
pseudoClasses.detail: invalid, once the person has been through it
pseudoClasses.doc: Like `:invalid`, but only after the field was changed and left, or its form's submission was tried. The one to put error styling on.

pseudoClasses.name: first-child
pseudoClasses.doc: Counted among the elements drawn there, so a row an `r-if` leaves out is not counted. `:last-child` is not matched yet.

pseudoClasses.name: nth-child
pseudoClasses.detail: `:nth-child(an+b)`: by its place among its siblings
pseudoClasses.doc: Counted from 1: `odd`, `even`, `3`, `2n+1`, `-n+3`. The `of S` form is not read yet.

pseudoClasses.name: not
pseudoClasses.doc: Takes compound selectors (`.done`, `button:disabled`), separated by commas, and counts as specific as the most specific of them. A combinator inside (`:not(.a .b)`) is not read yet, and the rule never matches.

cssPropertyDocs.name: display
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how this box lays its children out
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `block` (the default), `flex`, `grid`, `inline` or `none`. **Rux defaults to `block`**, so a box does not lay its children out in a row until you say `display: flex`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: width
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how wide the box is
cssPropertyDocs.doc: A length or a percentage of the parent's width. A child of a flex column already fills its width, since the cross-axis default is `stretch`; `width` is for when it should not.

cssPropertyDocs.name: height
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how tall the box is
cssPropertyDocs.doc: A length or a percentage. A definite height is half of what makes a scroller; the other half is `overflow`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: gap
cssPropertyDocs.detail: space between children
cssPropertyDocs.doc: On a flex or grid parent. Space *between* items only, never outside them, which is what makes it different from margin.

cssPropertyDocs.name: min-width
cssPropertyDocs.detail: a width it will not go under
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Stops a flex item shrinking past this. `min-width: 0` is the escape hatch when an item refuses to shrink at all.

cssPropertyDocs.name: max-width
cssPropertyDocs.detail: a width it will not go over
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Caps the box however much room there is. Common on text so a line does not run the full window.

cssPropertyDocs.name: min-height
cssPropertyDocs.detail: a height it will not go under
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Useful on a scroller that must keep its size when empty.

cssPropertyDocs.name: max-height
cssPropertyDocs.detail: a height it will not go over
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Caps growth; pair with `overflow` to scroll the excess rather than clip it.

cssPropertyDocs.name: padding
cssPropertyDocs.detail: space inside the border, all four sides
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One to four lengths, clockwise from the top. Inside the background, so padding is painted in the box's own colour.

cssPropertyDocs.name: padding-top
cssPropertyDocs.detail: space inside the top edge
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Overrides the `padding` shorthand for this side.

cssPropertyDocs.name: padding-right
cssPropertyDocs.detail: space inside the right edge
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Overrides the `padding` shorthand for this side.

cssPropertyDocs.name: padding-bottom
cssPropertyDocs.detail: space inside the bottom edge
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Overrides the `padding` shorthand for this side.

cssPropertyDocs.name: padding-left
cssPropertyDocs.detail: space inside the left edge
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Overrides the `padding` shorthand for this side.

cssPropertyDocs.name: margin
cssPropertyDocs.detail: space outside the box, all four sides
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One to four lengths, clockwise from the top. Outside the background, so it shows the parent through.

cssPropertyDocs.name: margin-top
cssPropertyDocs.detail: space outside the top edge
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Overrides the `margin` shorthand for this side.

cssPropertyDocs.name: margin-right
cssPropertyDocs.detail: space outside the right edge
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Overrides the `margin` shorthand for this side.

cssPropertyDocs.name: margin-bottom
cssPropertyDocs.detail: space outside the bottom edge
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Overrides the `margin` shorthand for this side.

cssPropertyDocs.name: margin-left
cssPropertyDocs.detail: space outside the left edge
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Overrides the `margin` shorthand for this side.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border
cssPropertyDocs.detail: width, style and colour of the outline
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `2px solid #45475a`. The style word is accepted and only the width and colour are drawn.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-width
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how thick the outline is
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Takes room in the layout, so changing it moves the content inside.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-color
cssPropertyDocs.detail: what colour the outline is
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Animatable, so it is the usual way to show focus without the box moving.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-radius
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how round the corners are
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One to four lengths, grouped by diagonal. Takes a percentage, resolved against the box's shorter side, so `50%` rounds a square into a circle and an oblong into a pill. Clips the background and the border; it does **not** clip children unless the box also has `overflow: hidden`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-top-left-radius
cssPropertyDocs.detail: roundness of one corner
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Overrides `border-radius` for this corner.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-top-right-radius
cssPropertyDocs.detail: roundness of one corner
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Overrides `border-radius` for this corner.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-bottom-right-radius
cssPropertyDocs.detail: roundness of one corner
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Overrides `border-radius` for this corner.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-bottom-left-radius
cssPropertyDocs.detail: roundness of one corner
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Overrides `border-radius` for this corner.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-top
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the top edge's width and colour
cssPropertyDocs.doc: The one-side form of the `border` shorthand.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-right
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the right edge's width and colour
cssPropertyDocs.doc: The one-side form of the `border` shorthand.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-bottom
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the bottom edge's width and colour
cssPropertyDocs.doc: The one-side form of the `border` shorthand. A cheap way to draw a divider under a row.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-left
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the left edge's width and colour
cssPropertyDocs.doc: The one-side form of the `border` shorthand. A cheap way to draw a quote bar.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-top-width
cssPropertyDocs.detail: thickness of the top edge
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Set on its own, leaving the colour to the shorthand.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-right-width
cssPropertyDocs.detail: thickness of the right edge
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Set on its own, leaving the colour to the shorthand.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-bottom-width
cssPropertyDocs.detail: thickness of the bottom edge
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Set on its own, leaving the colour to the shorthand.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-left-width
cssPropertyDocs.detail: thickness of the left edge
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Set on its own, leaving the colour to the shorthand.

cssPropertyDocs.name: overflow
cssPropertyDocs.detail: what happens to content too big for the box
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `auto` or `scroll` makes this box **the scroller**; `hidden` or `clip` cuts the overflow off. **Nothing in Rux scrolls until a box is told to**, and the box told is the one with a definite size.

cssPropertyDocs.name: overflow-x
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the same, for the horizontal axis only
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Use when a row should scroll sideways while the page does not.

cssPropertyDocs.name: overflow-y
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the same, for the vertical axis only
cssPropertyDocs.doc: The usual half: a list that scrolls while the screen around it stays put.

cssPropertyDocs.name: overscroll-behavior
cssPropertyDocs.detail: whether scrolling past the end passes outward
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `auto` (the default) lets what this scroller cannot take go on to the scroller around it, so a list at its end lets the page scroll. `contain` or `none` keeps it here. One value for both axes, or `x y`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: overscroll-behavior-x
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the same, sideways only
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `auto`, `contain` or `none`, for the horizontal axis.

cssPropertyDocs.name: overscroll-behavior-y
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the same, up and down only
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `auto`, `contain` or `none`, for the vertical axis: a panel whose list should never scroll the page behind it.

cssPropertyDocs.name: scrollbar-width
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how thick the scrollbars are drawn
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `auto`, `thin`, or `none`, which draws no bar while the box still scrolls. Bars show while the box scrolls or the pointer is over it, then fade.

cssPropertyDocs.name: scrollbar-color
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the scrollbars' thumb and track colours
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Two colours, thumb then track, or `auto` for the default grey.

cssPropertyDocs.name: clip-path
cssPropertyDocs.detail: cut the box to a shape
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `circle()`, `ellipse()`, `inset(… round …)`, `polygon()`, `path()`, `xywh()` or `rect()`, over `border-box` (the default), `padding-box`, `content-box` or `margin-box`. The box and everything in it are cut; taps are not yet.

cssPropertyDocs.name: mask-image
cssPropertyDocs.detail: show the box only where an image or gradient is
cssPropertyDocs.doc: A gradient or `url()`, laid over the border box: the box and everything in it show where the mask is opaque, and fade where it fades. `mask-mode: luminance` uses how light it is instead. An image covers the box, as `background-image` does.

cssPropertyDocs.name: mask
cssPropertyDocs.detail: mask-image and mask-mode at once
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `mask: linear-gradient(black, transparent)`, and `luminance` to mask by lightness.

cssPropertyDocs.name: mask-mode
cssPropertyDocs.detail: mask by opacity or by lightness
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `alpha` (and `match-source`, the default) or `luminance`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-style
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how the border's line is drawn
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `solid`, `dashed`, `dotted`, `double`, `groove`, `ridge`, `inset`, `outset`, `hidden` or `none`, one to four values like `margin`. **A border with no style draws nothing**, as in CSS: write `border: 2px solid red`, not `border: 2px red`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-top-style
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how the top edge is drawn
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One of the `border-style` values, for that side alone.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-right-style
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how the right edge is drawn
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One of the `border-style` values, for that side alone.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-bottom-style
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how the bottom edge is drawn
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One of the `border-style` values, for that side alone.

cssPropertyDocs.name: border-left-style
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how the left edge is drawn
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One of the `border-style` values, for that side alone.

cssPropertyDocs.name: text-shadow
cssPropertyDocs.detail: a shadow or glow under the text
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `x y blur colour`, and a comma list of them, the first on top. Inherited. With no colour it is the text's own: `text-shadow: 0 0 8px` glows in the text colour.

cssPropertyDocs.name: filter
cssPropertyDocs.detail: blur or recolour the box and everything in it
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `blur()`, `brightness()`, `contrast()`, `drop-shadow()`, `grayscale()`, `hue-rotate()`, `invert()`, `opacity()`, `saturate()` and `sepia()`, applied in the order written.

cssPropertyDocs.name: backdrop-filter
cssPropertyDocs.detail: blur or recolour what is behind the box
cssPropertyDocs.doc: The same functions as `filter`, applied to what is drawn behind the box and shown inside it: `backdrop-filter: blur(12px)` is frosted glass. Give the box a translucent background to see it.

cssPropertyDocs.name: mix-blend-mode
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how the box blends with what is under it
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `multiply`, `screen`, `overlay`, `darken`, `lighten`, `color-dodge`, `color-burn`, `hard-light`, `soft-light`, `difference`, `exclusion`, `hue`, `saturation`, `color` or `luminosity`. The box and everything in it blend as one layer.

cssPropertyDocs.name: opacity
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how see-through the whole box is
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `0` to `1`, and it applies to the **subtree**, not just this box. Animatable, and the cheapest thing to animate.

cssPropertyDocs.name: cursor
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the pointer shape over this box
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Only `pointer` differs from the default arrow. Applied by the shell on hover.

cssPropertyDocs.name: touch-action
cssPropertyDocs.detail: which axes a finger may still scroll here
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Decides who wins when a `@drag` and a scroller want the same finger. The default `auto` lets the scroller keep any axis it can actually scroll, so a drag inside a scrolling list does not trap the page; `none` gives the element the finger outright; `pan-x` and `pan-y` keep one axis for the scroller. Settled once, when the finger passes the drag threshold. Touch only: a mouse scrolls by wheel, not by dragging.

cssPropertyDocs.name: box-shadow
cssPropertyDocs.detail: a shadow cast by the box
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `x y blur spread colour`, and a comma list of them, the first on top. Painted outside the border, or with `inset` inside it over the background, and takes no space in the layout. With no colour it is the text `color`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: outline
cssPropertyDocs.detail: a line around the box, outside its border
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `width style colour`, in any order. Takes no space, is drawn over the element's content, and follows `border-radius`. The focus ring is the default `:focus-visible { outline: auto }`, so this is also how it is restyled or removed. Solid lines only: `dashed` and `dotted` are drawn solid, with a warning.

cssPropertyDocs.name: outline-color
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the outline's colour
cssPropertyDocs.doc: The element's own `color` when not written, as CSS's `currentColor`. On the focus ring alone, it recolours the ring and keeps its shape.

cssPropertyDocs.name: outline-offset
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the gap between the border and the outline
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `0` by default. Negative draws the outline inside the box.

cssPropertyDocs.name: outline-style
cssPropertyDocs.detail: whether and how the outline is drawn
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `none` (the initial value), `solid`, or `auto`, the platform's focus ring.

cssPropertyDocs.name: outline-width
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the outline's thickness
cssPropertyDocs.doc: A length, or `thin`, `medium` (the initial, 3px) or `thick`. `0` removes the outline.

cssPropertyDocs.name: transform
cssPropertyDocs.detail: move, rotate or scale the painted box
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `translate`, `rotate`, `scale`, composed left to right. Paint-only, so it never moves anything else. **A transformed box becomes the containing block** for `absolute` *and* `fixed` descendants, which is why a `fixed` child stops being fixed inside one.

cssPropertyDocs.name: transition
cssPropertyDocs.detail: animate a property when it changes
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `<property> <duration> <easing>`, comma-separated for more than one. Only some properties can animate; naming one that cannot is a warning rather than silence.

cssPropertyDocs.name: flex
cssPropertyDocs.detail: grow, shrink and basis in one
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `flex: 1` means `1 1 0%`, not `1 1 auto`. The usual way to say \"take the leftover room\".

cssPropertyDocs.name: flex-grow
cssPropertyDocs.detail: share of the spare room this item takes
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `0` (the default) means it never grows.

cssPropertyDocs.name: flex-shrink
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how readily this item gives room up
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `0` stops it shrinking below its content.

cssPropertyDocs.name: flex-basis
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the size to start from before growing
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `auto` uses the item's own size; a length overrides it.

cssPropertyDocs.name: flex-wrap
cssPropertyDocs.detail: whether items may move onto another line
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `wrap` or `wrap-reverse` allow it; anything else keeps one line.

cssPropertyDocs.name: flex-direction
cssPropertyDocs.detail: which way the children are laid out
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `row` (the default) or `column`. This is the axis every alignment property below is described against.

cssPropertyDocs.name: justify-content
cssPropertyDocs.detail: alignment along the main axis
cssPropertyDocs.doc: The axis `flex-direction` set. On a `row`, this is horizontal.

cssPropertyDocs.name: align-items
cssPropertyDocs.detail: alignment across the main axis
cssPropertyDocs.doc: On a `row`, this is vertical. Defaults to `stretch`, as in CSS, so a child fills the cross axis. `align-self: flex-start` makes one child hug.

cssPropertyDocs.name: align-self
cssPropertyDocs.detail: this one item's cross-axis alignment
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Overrides the parent's `align-items` for this item only. `align-self: flex-end` is how one row in a list moves to the far side.

cssPropertyDocs.name: justify-self
cssPropertyDocs.detail: this one item's main-axis alignment
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Grid mostly; a single item's override.

cssPropertyDocs.name: justify-items
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the default main-axis alignment for children
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Grid mostly; set on the parent.

cssPropertyDocs.name: align-content
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how whole lines are spaced
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Only does anything with more than one line, so it needs `flex-wrap: wrap`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: row-gap
cssPropertyDocs.detail: space between rows
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Overrides `gap` on the vertical axis.

cssPropertyDocs.name: column-gap
cssPropertyDocs.detail: space between columns
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Overrides `gap` on the horizontal axis.

cssPropertyDocs.name: grid-template-columns
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the column tracks
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `repeat(3, 1fr)`, `200px 1fr`, and so on. Setting this is most of what makes a grid.

cssPropertyDocs.name: grid-template-rows
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the row tracks
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Explicit row sizes; rows beyond these come from `grid-auto-rows`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: grid-template-areas
cssPropertyDocs.detail: name the areas of a grid
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One string per row, one name per cell, `.` for an empty one: `"head head" "side main"`. Each name must make a rectangle. Place an item with `grid-area: main`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: grid-template
cssPropertyDocs.detail: rows, columns and areas at once
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `<rows> / <columns>`, or with areas, each row's string then its size: `"head head" 60px "side main" 1fr / 200px 1fr`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: grid-area
cssPropertyDocs.detail: which area this item fills
cssPropertyDocs.doc: An area name from `grid-template-areas`, or `row-start / column-start / row-end / column-end`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: grid-column
cssPropertyDocs.detail: which columns this item spans
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `grid-column: 1 / 3`, or `span 2`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: grid-row
cssPropertyDocs.detail: which rows this item spans
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `grid-row: 1 / 3`, or `span 2`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: grid-column-start
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the column this item starts at
cssPropertyDocs.doc: The longhand half of `grid-column`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: grid-column-end
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the column this item ends at
cssPropertyDocs.doc: The longhand half of `grid-column`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: grid-row-start
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the row this item starts at
cssPropertyDocs.doc: The longhand half of `grid-row`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: grid-row-end
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the row this item ends at
cssPropertyDocs.doc: The longhand half of `grid-row`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: grid-auto-flow
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how items without a place are filled in
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `row` or `column`, plus `dense` to backfill gaps.

cssPropertyDocs.name: grid-auto-rows
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the size of rows nobody declared
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Applies to rows created beyond `grid-template-rows`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: grid-auto-columns
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the size of columns nobody declared
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Applies to columns created beyond `grid-template-columns`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: position
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how this box is placed
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `static` (the default), `relative`, `sticky`, `absolute` or `fixed`. **All five are honored as of v0.7**; before that four of them parsed and silently behaved as `relative`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: top
cssPropertyDocs.detail: distance from the top edge
cssPropertyDocs.doc: An offset for `relative`/`absolute`/`fixed`, and a **threshold** for `sticky`: where it stops and holds.

cssPropertyDocs.name: right
cssPropertyDocs.detail: distance from the right edge
cssPropertyDocs.doc: An offset, or a sticky threshold. `absolute` measures from the nearest positioned ancestor, not the parent.

cssPropertyDocs.name: bottom
cssPropertyDocs.detail: distance from the bottom edge
cssPropertyDocs.doc: An offset, or a sticky threshold.

cssPropertyDocs.name: left
cssPropertyDocs.detail: distance from the left edge
cssPropertyDocs.doc: An offset, or a sticky threshold.

cssPropertyDocs.name: aspect-ratio
cssPropertyDocs.detail: width-to-height ratio to keep
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `16 / 9`. Gives a box a height derived from its width, so a media box keeps its shape as it resizes.

cssPropertyDocs.name: z-index
cssPropertyDocs.detail: which box is drawn over which
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `auto` or a whole number. Counts on a positioned box and on a flex or grid item; higher is drawn over lower, inside the same stacking context. A `fixed` box is **not** on top by itself: give it a `z-index`. Animates in whole steps.

cssPropertyDocs.name: isolation
cssPropertyDocs.detail: start a stacking context
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `isolate` makes this box a stacking context and does nothing else, so a `z-index` inside it, negative ones included, is sorted inside it and never escapes.

cssPropertyDocs.name: anchor-name
cssPropertyDocs.detail: name this box as an anchor
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `--menu-button`. Another box can then be placed against it with `position-anchor` and `anchor()`. Names are document-wide, so a component can anchor to a box anywhere; when two boxes share a name the later one is the anchor.

cssPropertyDocs.name: position-anchor
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the anchor this box is placed against
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `--menu-button`, on an `absolute` or `fixed` box. Then `top: anchor(bottom); left: anchor(left)` puts it under that box, and it follows the box when a panel scrolls. `fixed` also escapes every `overflow` clip, which is how a dropdown gets out of a scrolling panel. When the anchor scrolls out of view the box is not drawn.
cssPropertyDocs.usage: .menu { position: fixed; position-anchor: --row-menu; top: anchor(bottom); left: anchor(left); }

cssPropertyDocs.name: position-try-fallbacks
cssPropertyDocs.detail: other places to try when an anchored box does not fit
cssPropertyDocs.doc: A comma-separated list: `flip-block` (above instead of below), `flip-inline` (left instead of right), `flip-start`, or a `@position-try --name { … }` rule's name. The first that fits wins; with none, the box's own place. A fallback that fitted is kept while it still fits.

cssPropertyDocs.name: position-try-order
cssPropertyDocs.detail: which fallback with the most room wins
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `normal` tries them in order. `most-width` / `most-height` (or `most-inline-size` / `most-block-size`) try the places with the most room on that axis first.

cssPropertyDocs.name: position-try
cssPropertyDocs.detail: fallback places, shorthand
cssPropertyDocs.doc: An optional `position-try-order`, then `position-try-fallbacks`: `position-try: most-height flip-block`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: content-visibility
cssPropertyDocs.detail: skip a box's contents while it is off screen
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `auto` lays out and draws the contents only while the box is near the screen, which is how a list of thousands of rows stays fast: put it on each row with `contain-intrinsic-size`. `hidden` always skips them. Either way the box clips its contents and is a stacking context.

cssPropertyDocs.name: contain-intrinsic-size
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the size a skipped box takes
cssPropertyDocs.doc: With `content-visibility`, the size standing in for skipped contents. `auto 40px` is 40px until the box has been drawn, then the size it was last drawn at. One value for both axes, or width then height.

cssPropertyDocs.name: contain-intrinsic-width
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the width a skipped box takes
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One axis of `contain-intrinsic-size`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: contain-intrinsic-height
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the height a skipped box takes
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One axis of `contain-intrinsic-size`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: contain-intrinsic-inline-size
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the width a skipped box takes
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `contain-intrinsic-width`, by its logical name.

cssPropertyDocs.name: contain-intrinsic-block-size
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the height a skipped box takes
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `contain-intrinsic-height`, by its logical name.

cssPropertyDocs.name: background
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the colour and images behind the content
cssPropertyDocs.doc: A colour, and layers of `linear-gradient(…)`, `radial-gradient(…)` or `url(…)`, each with its position, `/ size`, repeat, attachment and boxes, as in CSS. Sets every `background-*` longhand.

cssPropertyDocs.name: background-color
cssPropertyDocs.detail: a flat colour behind the content
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Animatable, so it is what a hover or pressed state usually changes.

cssPropertyDocs.name: background-image
cssPropertyDocs.detail: images behind the content
cssPropertyDocs.doc: A comma list of `linear-gradient`, `radial-gradient` and `url(…)`, the first on top. An image is its natural size, tiled, unless `background-size` says otherwise.

cssPropertyDocs.name: background-size
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how large each background image is
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `cover`, `contain`, or a width and height as lengths, percentages of the box or `auto`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: background-position
cssPropertyDocs.detail: where each background image sits
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One to four values: `center`, `right 10px bottom 20px`, `25% 75%`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: background-position-x
cssPropertyDocs.detail: where each background image sits across
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `left`, `center`, `right`, an offset, or `right 10px`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: background-position-y
cssPropertyDocs.detail: where each background image sits down
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `top`, `center`, `bottom`, an offset, or `bottom 10px`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: background-repeat
cssPropertyDocs.detail: whether a background image tiles
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `repeat`, `no-repeat`, `repeat-x`, `repeat-y`, `space` or `round`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: background-clip
cssPropertyDocs.detail: which box a background is cut to
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `border-box` (the default), `padding-box` or `content-box`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: background-origin
cssPropertyDocs.detail: which box a background is placed in
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `padding-box` (the default), `border-box` or `content-box`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: background-attachment
cssPropertyDocs.detail: what a background moves with
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `scroll` (the box), `fixed` (the window) or `local` (the box's scrolled content).

cssPropertyDocs.name: accent-color
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the colour a control is drawn in
cssPropertyDocs.doc: A switch's track when on, and a slider's fill and thumb. Not inherited.

cssPropertyDocs.name: color
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the colour of the text
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Inherited, so setting it on a container covers the text inside. Animatable.

cssPropertyDocs.name: font-size
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how large the text is
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Also the reference for `em` on this box, so changing it moves anything sized in `em`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: font-weight
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how heavy the text is
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `normal`, `bold`, `lighter`, `bolder`, or a number from 100 to 900.

cssPropertyDocs.name: font-family
cssPropertyDocs.detail: which typeface to use
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Falls back through the list to whatever the system has.

cssPropertyDocs.name: font-style
cssPropertyDocs.detail: upright or italic
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `italic` and `oblique` both slant; anything else is upright.

cssPropertyDocs.name: text-align
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how lines sit within the box
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `start`, `center`, `end`/`right`, or `justify`. Aligns the **lines inside** the box, which is not the same as moving the box.

cssPropertyDocs.name: letter-spacing
cssPropertyDocs.detail: extra space between characters
cssPropertyDocs.doc: A length, positive or negative.

cssPropertyDocs.name: word-spacing
cssPropertyDocs.detail: extra space between words
cssPropertyDocs.doc: A length, positive or negative.

cssPropertyDocs.name: line-height
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the height of one line of text
cssPropertyDocs.doc: A number (a multiple of the font size) or a length. The usual way to give body text room to breathe.

cssPropertyDocs.name: direction
cssPropertyDocs.detail: which way text and rows run
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `ltr` (the default) or `rtl`, inherited; the `dir` attribute sets it too, and a rule wins over the attribute. Under `rtl` a flex row starts from the right, grid columns count from the right, `text-align: start` is the right edge, and the logical properties (`margin-inline-start` and the rest) take the right side as their start.

cssPropertyDocs.name: visibility
cssPropertyDocs.detail: hide a box but keep its place
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `hidden` draws nothing and takes no tap or focus, but the box keeps its space, unlike `display: none`. Inherited: a child can be `visible` inside a hidden box. `collapse` is `hidden`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: color-scheme
cssPropertyDocs.detail: which side of light-dark() colours take
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `light dark` follows the system's light or dark setting, `dark` is always dark, and `normal` (the default) is light whatever the system says, as in CSS. Inherited, so setting it on the screen sets it for the page.

cssPropertyDocs.name: margin-inline
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the margins at the start and end of the line
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One value for both, or the start's then the end's. Start is left under `ltr` and right under `rtl`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: margin-inline-start
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the margin where a line starts
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Left under `ltr`, right under `rtl`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: margin-inline-end
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the margin where a line ends
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Right under `ltr`, left under `rtl`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: margin-block
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the top and bottom margins
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One value for both, or the top's then the bottom's.

cssPropertyDocs.name: margin-block-start
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the top margin
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Rux writes horizontally, so the block start is always the top.

cssPropertyDocs.name: margin-block-end
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the bottom margin
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Always the bottom.

cssPropertyDocs.name: padding-inline
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the padding at the start and end of the line
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One value for both, or the start's then the end's.

cssPropertyDocs.name: padding-inline-start
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the padding where a line starts
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Left under `ltr`, right under `rtl`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: padding-inline-end
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the padding where a line ends
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Right under `ltr`, left under `rtl`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: padding-block
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the top and bottom padding
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One value for both, or the top's then the bottom's.

cssPropertyDocs.name: padding-block-start
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the top padding
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Always the top.

cssPropertyDocs.name: padding-block-end
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the bottom padding
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Always the bottom.

cssPropertyDocs.name: inset-inline
cssPropertyDocs.detail: `left` and `right` by the direction
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One value for both, or the start's then the end's.

cssPropertyDocs.name: inset-inline-start
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the offset from the start side
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `left` under `ltr`, `right` under `rtl`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: inset-inline-end
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the offset from the end side
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `right` under `ltr`, `left` under `rtl`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: inset-block
cssPropertyDocs.detail: `top` and `bottom`
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One value for both, or the top's then the bottom's.

cssPropertyDocs.name: inset-block-start
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the same as `top`
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Always the top.

cssPropertyDocs.name: inset-block-end
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the same as `bottom`
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Always the bottom.

cssPropertyDocs.name: vertical-align
cssPropertyDocs.detail: where a box in a line of text sits
cssPropertyDocs.doc: For an `<image>` or `<path>` inside a `<text>`. `baseline` (the default) stands it on the baseline, so an icon as tall as the text sits high; `middle` centres it on the text, which is usually what an icon wants; `text-top` and `text-bottom` line it up with the top or bottom of the text.

cssPropertyDocs.name: white-space
cssPropertyDocs.detail: whether runs of space collapse and lines wrap
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `normal` and `nowrap` turn every run of spaces, tabs and newlines into one space, as CSS does; `pre` and `pre-wrap` keep them all; `pre-line` keeps newlines only, the one for text from data whose line breaks matter. `nowrap` and `pre` keep the text on one line.

cssPropertyDocs.name: text-decoration
cssPropertyDocs.detail: lines over, under or through the text
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Its lines (`underline`, `overline`, `line-through`), style, colour and thickness, in any order.

cssPropertyDocs.name: text-decoration-line
cssPropertyDocs.detail: which decoration to draw
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `underline`, `overline` and `line-through`, any of them together.

cssPropertyDocs.name: text-decoration-color
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the colour of the decoration
cssPropertyDocs.doc: The text's own colour when not set.

cssPropertyDocs.name: text-decoration-style
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how the decoration is drawn
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `solid`, `double`, `dotted`, `dashed` or `wavy`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: text-decoration-thickness
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how thick the decoration is
cssPropertyDocs.doc: A length, or `auto` for the font's own.

cssPropertyDocs.name: text-underline-offset
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how far below the baseline the underline is
cssPropertyDocs.doc: A length, or `auto` for the font's own.

cssPropertyDocs.name: text-transform
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the text in capitals or small letters
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `uppercase`, `lowercase` or `capitalize`. Inherited.

cssPropertyDocs.name: text-indent
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how far in the first line starts
cssPropertyDocs.doc: A length or a percentage of the width, with `hanging` to indent every line but the first, and `each-line`. Inherited.

cssPropertyDocs.name: text-overflow
cssPropertyDocs.detail: what a line too long for its box ends in
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `ellipsis` ends it in `…`. Needs `overflow: hidden` and `white-space: nowrap`, as in CSS.
cssPropertyDocs.usage: .name { white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; }

cssPropertyDocs.name: font-variant
cssPropertyDocs.detail: small capitals, numerals and ligatures
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Any of the `font-variant-*` keywords; the font's own OpenType features.

cssPropertyDocs.name: font-variant-caps
cssPropertyDocs.detail: small capitals
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `small-caps`, `all-small-caps`, `petite-caps` and the rest, when the font has them.

cssPropertyDocs.name: font-variant-numeric
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how numerals are drawn
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `tabular-nums` for columns that line up, `oldstyle-nums`, fractions, `ordinal`, `slashed-zero`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: font-variant-ligatures
cssPropertyDocs.detail: which ligatures the font joins
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `none`, `no-common-ligatures`, `discretionary-ligatures` and the rest.

cssPropertyDocs.name: font-variant-position
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the font's own subscripts and superscripts
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `sub` or `super`, when the font has them.

cssPropertyDocs.name: font-variant-east-asian
cssPropertyDocs.detail: East Asian glyph forms
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `jis78` to `jis04`, `simplified`, `traditional`, `full-width`, `proportional-width`, `ruby`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: font-feature-settings
cssPropertyDocs.detail: OpenType features by tag
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `"tnum"`, `"liga" 0`: drawn after `font-variant`, so it wins where they meet.

cssPropertyDocs.name: font-variation-settings
cssPropertyDocs.detail: a variable font's axes by tag

cssPropertyDocs.name: font-stretch
cssPropertyDocs.detail: a narrower or wider face
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `condensed` to `expanded`, or a percentage, from the font's width axis or its narrow and wide faces.

cssPropertyDocs.name: font-width
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the newer name of `font-stretch`
cssPropertyDocs.doc: The same values.

cssPropertyDocs.name: caret-color
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the colour of a field's caret
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `auto` is the text's colour. Inherited.

cssPropertyDocs.name: object-fit
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how an image fills its box
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `fill` (stretched, the default), `contain`, `cover`, `none` or `scale-down`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: object-position
cssPropertyDocs.detail: where an image sits in its box
cssPropertyDocs.doc: One to four values, as `background-position`: `left`, `right 8px bottom 8px`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: pointer-events
cssPropertyDocs.detail: whether a pointer can reach the box
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `none` lets a tap through to what is under it; the keyboard still reaches it. Inherited.

cssPropertyDocs.name: scroll-behavior
cssPropertyDocs.detail: whether a scroll asked for glides
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `smooth` on a scroller: `scrollIntoView()` and Tab glide there. A wheel or a finger never does.

cssPropertyDocs.name: overflow-wrap
cssPropertyDocs.detail: whether a long word may break mid-word
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `break-word` or `anywhere` let an unbreakable word break rather than overflow.

cssPropertyDocs.name: word-wrap
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the older name for `overflow-wrap`
cssPropertyDocs.doc: Accepted as a synonym.

cssPropertyDocs.name: word-break
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how aggressively words break
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `break-all` breaks anywhere at all, not only to avoid an overflow.

cssPropertyDocs.name: fill
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the colour inside the path
cssPropertyDocs.doc: On `<path>`. Paint is CSS here rather than an SVG attribute, which is what gives a path `:hover`, `:class` and `transition`. Animatable.

cssPropertyDocs.name: fill-rule
cssPropertyDocs.detail: which parts count as inside
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `nonzero` (the default) or `evenodd`. The difference shows on a shape that crosses itself, like a star.

cssPropertyDocs.name: stroke
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the colour of the outline
cssPropertyDocs.doc: On `<path>`. Animatable.

cssPropertyDocs.name: stroke-width
cssPropertyDocs.detail: how thick the outline is
cssPropertyDocs.doc: On `<path>`. Animatable, so a line can thicken on hover.

cssPropertyDocs.name: stroke-linecap
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the shape of a line's ends
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `butt` (the default), `round` or `square`.

cssPropertyDocs.name: stroke-linejoin
cssPropertyDocs.detail: the shape where two segments meet
cssPropertyDocs.doc: `miter` (the default), `round` or `bevel`.
